source_title: XP Power Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 105 and 155 state that the Directors' report and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 3 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 2% to £199.9m but fell 2% in constant currency and 4% like for like. Statutory operating profit fell 32% to £26.7m, adjusted operating profit declined 16% and adjusted margin contracted to 18.0% from 22.0%, reflecting semiconductor weakness, tariffs, product mix and investment. Conversely, operating cash rose 72% to £46.2m, free cash flow reached £26.2m, net debt fell 21% to £41.3m and leverage was 0.92x.
already_announced_exclusion: The ERP implementation, Fyfield design-centre closure, Nevada-to-Vietnam manufacturing transfer and associated restructuring disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Material earnings and margin deterioration creates significant pressure despite modest reported revenue growth. Strong cash generation, falling debt, low leverage and broad growth outside semiconductors provide substantial contrary evidence.

source_title: XP Power Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report page 180 states that the financial statements were authorised by Board resolution on 1 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 3% to £240.3m and 10% in constant currency, supported by semiconductor demand and a record order book. Statutory operating profit fell 21% to £29.7m and margin contracted to 12.4% from 16.0% amid supply constraints, currency effects and investment. Operating cash remained strong at £36.4m with 122% conversion and free cash flow of £12.5m, while net debt rose modestly to £24.6m.
already_announced_exclusion: The ERP upgrade, manufacturing-capacity programme and other operational changes disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Profit and margin contraction amid severe supply-chain constraints creates material pressure. Revenue growth, record demand, strong cash conversion, positive free cash flow and a modest absolute debt position provide substantial contrary evidence.

source_title: XP Power Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 21 and 106 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved or authorised by the Board on 4 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 9% in constant currency to £316.4m, but order intake collapsed to £208.8m and book-to-bill to 0.66x as semiconductor demand slowed. Adjusted operating profit fell to £38.1m and margin to 12.0%. Unexpected site-relocation spending and weaker trading left insufficient covenant headroom, prompting cost and capex reductions, dividend suspension, a £44.0m share placing and amended banking covenants. The funding plan reduced net debt to £112.7m and leverage to 2.0x by year-end.
already_announced_exclusion: The comprehensive funding plan, cost-base restructuring, capex reductions, dividend suspension, share placing, facility relocations, supply-chain transformation and manufacturing transfers disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Acute covenant pressure, emergency funding actions, collapsing orders, lower profit and announced restructuring create exceptionally high pressure. Revenue growth, strong cash conversion and year-end deleveraging provide limited contrary evidence.
